title: Inverted index
body: An inverted index maps every term to the list of documents that contain it. Search engines use an inverted index to avoid scanning every document.

title: BM25 ranking function
body: BM25 is a ranking function that scores documents by term frequency, inverse document frequency and document length. It is the default similarity in Elasticsearch and Lucene.

title: TF-IDF
body: TF-IDF weighs a term by how often it appears in a document and how rare it is across the collection. It was the classic ranking method before BM25.

title: Elasticsearch
body: Elasticsearch is a distributed search and analytics engine built on Apache Lucene. It stores JSON documents in indices split into shards and replicas.

title: Apache Lucene
body: Lucene is a Java library for full text search. It provides indexing, analyzers, query parsing and ranking, and it powers Elasticsearch and Solr.

title: Tokenization
body: Tokenization splits text into tokens such as words. Analyzers combine a tokenizer with filters for lowercasing, stopwords and stemming.

title: Stemming
body: Stemming reduces words to a common root so that running, runs and run match each other. The Porter stemmer is a well known algorithm.

title: Stopwords
body: Stopwords are very common words such as the, and, of. Removing them shrinks the index and reduces noise in ranking.

title: Levenshtein distance
body: The Levenshtein edit distance counts insertions, deletions and substitutions needed to turn one word into another. Fuzzy search uses it to tolerate typos.

title: Precision and recall
body: Precision is the share of returned results that are relevant. Recall is the share of relevant documents that were returned.

title: nDCG
body: Normalized discounted cumulative gain measures ranking quality. Relevant results near the top of the list count more than results further down.

title: Sharding
body: Sharding splits an index across several machines so a search engine can scale horizontally. Each shard is a self contained Lucene index.

title: Autocomplete
body: Autocomplete suggests completions while the user types. Elasticsearch offers completion suggesters and edge n-gram analyzers for search as you type.

title: Faceted search
body: Faceted search lets users filter results by category, price or date. Elasticsearch implements facets with aggregations.

title: Phrase queries
body: A phrase query matches terms that appear next to each other in order. Positional information stored in the inverted index makes phrase search possible.

title: Web crawler
body: A web crawler downloads pages, follows links and feeds documents to the indexer. Crawlers must respect robots.txt and rate limits.

title: PageRank
body: PageRank ranks web pages by the links pointing to them. A link from an important page counts more than a link from an obscure one.

title: Vector search
body: Vector search finds documents whose embeddings are close to the query embedding. It captures meaning rather than exact words and complements keyword ranking.

title: Hybrid search
body: Hybrid search combines keyword ranking such as BM25 with vector similarity, often by reciprocal rank fusion, to get the best of both.

title: Caching search results
body: Search engines cache popular queries and filter results in memory so repeated searches return in milliseconds.

title: Cooking pasta
body: Boil salted water, add the pasta and stir. Cook until al dente, then drain and toss with sauce.

title: Running shoes
body: Good running shoes cushion the foot and support long runs. Replace them after several hundred kilometers.

title: Search engine optimization
body: Search engine optimization improves how a website ranks on public search engines through content, links and page speed.

title: Query parsing
body: Query parsing turns the text a user types into a structured query with terms, phrases, boolean operators and field filters.

title: Relevance tuning
body: Relevance tuning adjusts field boosts, synonyms and ranking parameters so the best documents appear first for real user queries.
